#9826. 17 apple dessert recipes for fall baking: Embrace the season with apple tarts, cookies, cakes, and more.

There’s an apple dessert for everyone. For the purists, there are lattice-topped pies and shingled galettes. For the non-traditionalists, there are caramel-frosted cakes and fritter-inspired loaves. And for apple lovers that hate cinnamon? Well, there are custardy cakes and classic French tarts. Ready to start baking with fall’s best fruit? Read on for our best apple dessert recipes.

There’s no shortage of apple in this cake — applesauce keeps things moist while boiled cider adds sharp, tangy fruit flavor. The cake is great on its own, but pair it with light, creamy Whipped Caramel Frosting, and you’ve got an irresistible baked version of a caramel apple (with none of the fears about your teeth).

Get the recipe: Whipped Caramel Apple Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vermont Boiled Cider

You only need one apple (and two people eager for an apple dessert) to make a pair of these adorable galettes. Half the apple is sliced, while the other half is grated, which creates a hidden layer of jam beneath the shingled slices. Flaky fruit tarts don’t get easier (or cuter!) than this.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

Get the recipe: Apple Cider Snickerdoodles

This super-easy one-bowl cake is loaded with chopped apples and walnuts, which give this moist, spiced cake heft and texture. The frosting, akin to a velvety brown sugar fudge, adds a textural counterpoint and an extra dimension of richness.

Get the recipe: Old-Fashioned Apple Cake with Brown Sugar Frosting

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" x 13" pan

Cinnamon and apple go together like a flannel and a beanie, but this recipe one-ups that perfect pairing with the addition of cinnamon chips. Diced apple and melty pockets of cinnamon-sugar are also studded throughout these autumnal scones, which are then finished off with an extra-crunchy sugar coating.

Get the recipe: Fresh Apple Cinnamon Scones

To make this recipe, you'll need: Cinnamon Sweet Bits

Ribbons of gooey, cinnamon-scented apples are twisted throughout this striking enriched loaf. Beautiful to behold (and easier to make than you’d think), this braided babka would be a welcome addition to any Rosh Hashanah table or fall celebration.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Baker’s Special Dry Milk

Spoiler alert: The eponymous secret ingredient in this special pie is boiled cider! Made by cooking down apple cider into a concentrate, a few drops deliver big apple flavor. When used in apple pies, it super-charges the fruit’s tart, tangy flavor, delivering a pie with over-the-top apple goodness.

Get the recipe: Secret Ingredient Apple Pie

To make this recipe, you'll need: Boiled Cider

If your go-to doughnut order is an apple fritter, this mash-up cake was made for you. The batter is made using the reverse creaming technique, which ensures a velvety crumb and tender texture. In each slice, there’s a filling and topping of cinnamon-dusted apples and a final drizzle of icy-white vanilla glaze. A slice rivals anything you can get at your local doughnut shop.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Instant ClearJel

This time of year, apples don't need much to make them shine. The paper-thin, crackly top layer of this cobbler highlights the juicy fruit beneath. It doesn’t need a lot of adornment, but a scoop of vanilla ice cream never hurt anything.

Get the recipe: Sugar-Crusted Apple Cobbler Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vietnamese Cinnamon

Is it a bar? A slab pie? Both! This breezy recipe swaps the flaky pastry for a buttery shortbread crust but keeps the warm, gooey apples and classic spices for a sliceable, portable dessert. To finish, there's a crumbly streusel topping inspired by Dutch apple pie.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

When you want a fruit dessert fast, you can always count on crisps — no rolling, no resting, and most importantly, no special equipment required! This crisp is made with a handful of baking basics, so when you find yourself with a surplus of apples, dessert is barely an hour away.

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" Square Pan

Beneath a buttery, apple-pie-spiced streusel lies a generous layer of tender apples, enriched with intensely flavored boiled cider for a filling that tastes like a truly great apple pie — rich, saucy, and fork-tender apples. The sour cream cake that surrounds the apple filling is plush, subtly tangy, and ultra-moist, providing the perfect counterpoint to the fruit filling and crumb topping.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

If you’re looking to veer from classic apple pie territory, this galette stays true to those roots but adds a few modern twists. It starts with a buttery whole wheat crust enriched with a touch of sour cream. Then, a layer of apple butter (which can be easily made by cooking down applesauce) is spread beneath a layer of artfully arranged apples slices.

Get the recipe: Apple Butter Apple Galette

To make this recipe, you'll need: Sparkling Sugar

There’s just enough batter to hold together a heap of sliced apples in this one-of-a-kind cake. Gently sweetened with brown sugar and scented with almond extract, this minimalist cake is greater than the sum of its parts — a sophisticated, custardy cake that’s deceivingly simple to make.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Almond Extract

This pull-apart bread is as fun to make as it is to eat. After rolling out the dough into a rectangle, it’s spread with sweetened apple filling. The dough is cut up into several strips, then stacked and squeezed into a loaf pan. It bakes into a loaf comprised of distinct slices of pillowy apple-studded bread that you can easily tear from the loaf.

Get the recipe: Cinnamon-Apple Pull-Apart Bread

To make this recipe, you'll need: SAF Instant Yeast

The French know a thing or two about baking with apples, and perhaps no recipe is as classic — or elegant — as the Tarte Tatin. Comprised of deeply caramelized apples layered over buttery pastry, it’s a dessert that stuns. Here, we've tested endlessly to ensure this sometimes-fussy dessert goes off without a hitch in your home kitchen.

Get the recipe: Classic Apple Tarte Tatin

To make this recipe, you'll need: King Arthur Round Cake Pan

These handheld treats harness all the nostalgia of a steaming hot McDonald’s fried apple pie but are infinitely better, thanks to the triple threat of a homemade flaky pie crust, a fresh apple filling amplified by boiled cider, and a generous coating of cinnamon sugar.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Boiled Cider and Apple Pie Spice

Are you looking for a new graphic design tool? Would you like to read a detailed review of Canva? As it's one of the tools I love using. I am also writing my first ebook using canva and publish it soon on my site you can download it is free.  Let's start the review.

Canva has a web version and also a mobile app

Canva is a free graphic design web application that allows you to create invitations, business cards, flyers, lesson plans, banners, and more using professionally designed templates. You can upload your own photos from your computer or from Google Drive, and add them to Canva's templates using a simple drag-and-drop interface. It's like having a basic version of Photoshop that doesn't require Graphic designing knowledge to use. It’s best for nongraphic designers.

Canva is a great tool for small business owners, online entrepreneurs, and marketers who don’t have the time and want to edit quickly.

To create sophisticated graphics, a tool such as Photoshop can is ideal. To use it, you’ll need to learn its hundreds of features, get familiar with the software, and it’s best to have a good background in design, too.

Also running the latest version of Photoshop you need a high-end computer.

So here  Canva takes place, with Canva you can do all that with drag-and-drop feature. It’s also easier to use and free. Also an even-more-affordable paid version is available for $12.95 per month.

The product is available in three plans: Free, Pro ($12.99/month per user or  $119.99/year for up to 5 people), and Enterprise ($30 per user per month, minimum 25 people).

To get started on Canva, you will need to create an account by providing your email address, Google, Facebook or Apple credentials. You will then choose your account type between student, teacher, small business, large company, non-profit, or personal. Based on your choice of account type, templates will be recommended to you.

You can sign up for a free trial of Canva Pro, or you can start with the free version to get a sense of whether it’s the right graphic design tool for your needs.

When you sign up for an account, Canva will suggest different post types to choose from. Based on the type of account you set up  you'll be able to see templates categorized by the following categories: social media posts, documents, presentations, marketing, events, ads, launch your business, build your online brand, etc.

Start by choosing a template for your post or searching for something more specific. Search by social network name to see a list of post types on each network.

Next, you can choose a template. Choose from hundreds of templates that are ready to go, with customizable photos, text, and other elements.

You can start your design by choosing from a variety of ready-made templates, searching for a template matching your needs, or working with a blank template.

Inside the Canva designer, the Elements tab gives you access to lines and shapes, graphics, photos, videos, audio, charts, photo frames, and photo grids.The search box on the Elements tab lets you search everything on Canva.

To begin with, Canva has a large library of elements to choose from. To find them, be specific in your search query. You may also want to search in the following tabs to see various elements separately:

The Photos tab lets you search for and choose from millions of professional stock photos for your templates.

You can replace the photos in our templates to create a new look. This can also make the template more suited to your industry.

You can find photos on other stock photography sites like pexel, pixabay and many more or simply upload your own photos.

When you choose an image, Canva’s photo editing features let you adjust the photo’s settings (brightness, contrast, saturation, etc.), crop, or animate it.

The Text tab lets you add headings, normal text, and graphical text to your design.

When you click on  text, you'll see options to adjust the font, font size, color, format, spacing, and text effects (like shadows).

Create an animated image or video by adding audio to capture user’s attention in social news feeds.

If you want to use audio from another stock site or your own audio tracks, you can upload them in the Uploads tab or from the more option.

Want to create your own videos? Choose from thousands of stock video clips. You’ll find videos that range upto 2 minutes

You can upload your own videos as well as videos from other stock sites in the Uploads tab.

Once you have chosen a video, you can use the editing features in Canva to trim the video, flip it, and adjust its transparency.

On the Background tab, you’ll find free stock photos to serve as backgrounds on your designs. Change out the background on a template to give it a more personal touch.

The Styles tab lets you quickly change the look and feel of your template with just a click. And if you have a Canva Pro subscription, you can upload your brand’s custom colors and fonts to ensure designs stay on brand.

If you have a Canva Pro subscription, you’ll have a Logos tab. Here, you can upload variations of your brand logo to use throughout your designs.

With Canva, you can also create your own logos. Note that you cannot trademark a logo with stock content in it.

With Canva, free users can download and share designs to multiple platforms including Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Slack and Tumblr.

Canva Pro allows you to work with your team on visual content. Designs can be created inside Canva, and then sent to your team members for approval. Everyone can make comments, edits, revisions, and keep track via the version history.

When it comes to printing your designs, Canva has you covered. With an extensive selection of printing options, they can turn your designs into anything from banners and wall art to mugs and t-shirts.

Canva Print is perfect for any business seeking to make a lasting impression. Create inspiring designs people will want to wear, keep, and share. Hand out custom business cards that leave a lasting impression on customers' minds.

The Canva app is available on the Apple App Store and Google Play. The Canva app has earned a 4.9 out of five star rating from over 946.3K Apple users and a 4.5 out of five star rating from over 6,996,708 Google users.

In addition to mobile apps, you can use Canva’s integration with other Internet services to add images and text from sources like Google Maps, Emojis, photos from Google Drive and Dropbox, YouTube videos, Flickr photos, Bitmojis, and other popular visual content elements.

In general, Canva is an excellent tool for those who need simple images for projects. If you are a graphic designer with experience, you will find Canva’s platform lacking in customization and advanced features – particularly vectors. But if you have little design experience, you will find Canva easier to use than advanced graphic design tools like Adobe Photoshop or Illustrator for most projects. #9821. I Played Three Mobile Games to Find the Math Hiding Inside Them

Games feel like pure fun, but every jump, camera swing and score counter is powered by math. For a class assignment I stopped playing like a player and started playing like a developer. I analysed three free mobile games: Subway Surfers and Vector from the recommended list, and Temple Run as my own pick. I looked for six ideas from class: distance, vectors, algebra, dot product, cross product and linear interpolation (lerp).

I can’t see the source code, so what follows is based on what I observed. Where I’m inferring how something works, I say “likely”.

I played each game for at least 30 minutes across 12 sessions, took screenshots and wrote notes as I went. You can also watch my video walkthrough: https://youtu.be/Mz7PZpl1Eoo

Quick facts: Mobile, endless runner, Kiloo and SYBO Games, 2012.

You play a graffiti artist running along train tracks, dodging trains and barriers while collecting coins. It is easy to learn (just swipe), speeds up gradually, and small missions keep giving you a reason to play one more run. My best run during testing scored 2,776, and a later run passed 6,000.

Distance: Score climbs as you travel forward, and coins are collected when you get close enough. A pickup check likely compares the gap between player and coin to a small radius: d = sqrt(dx^2 + dz^2) < r. Direction and vectors: The runner always has a forward velocity, plus sideways movement between three lanes. The forward speed grows over time, which is how the game gets harder. Algebra: The x2 multiplier, the coin counter and the mission bars (20/20 coins, 5/5 jumps) are all simple formulas. Score is roughly distance points times the multiplier, and mission progress is current / target. Dot product: Obstacles ahead matter and obstacles behind don’t. A check like forward . toObstacle > 0 would tell the game that something is in front of me. Cross product: Lane changes are left or right. The sign of the cross product of the forward direction and the direction to the target lane would tell the game which way to lean the character. Lerp: The runner glides between lanes instead of teleporting, and the camera follows smoothly.

When I swipe, the game likely sets a target lane, for example x = -1, 0 or +1 times the lane width. Every frame the runner moves a fraction of the way there:

x_new = x_current + (x_target - x_current) * t

That is lerp, and it is why the character glides. Jumping is probably simple physics: y(t) = v0*t - 0.5*g*t^2. Collision detection then compares the runner’s box with the boxes of trains and barriers. Since lanes are fixed, the game only has to check obstacles in the same lane, which keeps it fast on phones.

What works well: The controls are simple and responsive, the missions give clear short goals, and the bright colours make obstacles readable at high speed.

What I would improve: Fewer video-ad prompts on the mission screen, because they interrupt the flow. I would also add adaptive difficulty that adjusts obstacle patterns to how well the player has been doing, and a swipe sensitivity setting for different screen sizes.

Quick facts: Mobile, parkour platform runner, Nekki, 2012 . Vector is a 2D side-view parkour game. You control a silhouetted runner across rooftops, using a few on-screen buttons to jump, slide and vault. The art style and fluid animation are what make it enjoyable.

Distance: Bonus cubes (1/6 in the HUD) are collected when the runner reaches them, and the camera keeps the runner at a set distance on screen. Direction and vectors: In my screenshot the runner slides down a sloped roof, so the movement follows the slope, not a flat line. On a slope of angle theta the velocity is likely v = speed * (cos theta, -sin theta). Algebra: Collectible counters (cubes, objectives, coins), star ratings and unlock costs like 600 coins are numbers that increase or are compared to thresholds. Dot product: A dot product between the runner’s facing direction and the direction to an obstacle shows whether it is ahead, which could trigger a vault or slide. Cross product: The runner’s body tilts to match the roof. Aligning a character to a surface needs the surface normal, which comes from a cross product in 3D or a perpendicular in 2D. Lerp: Running, sliding and jumping blend into each other instead of snapping between poses, and the menu panels slide in smoothly.

One mechanic explained: sliding down a slope

The game needs the direction of the surface, the tangent vector t = (cos theta, -sin theta). Gravity pulls straight down, but only the part along the slope speeds the runner up. A dot product finds that part:

A steeper slope means a bigger sin theta, so the runner accelerates faster. The body is rotated to match the roof angle, and when the roof ends, the speed is kept and the runner enters a jump arc. That is why timing your tricks matters.

What works well: The silhouette against a detailed background keeps the runner easy to see, two buttons trigger many context-sensitive moves, and the cube and bonus goals encourage replaying levels.

What I would improve: A shorter step-by-step tutorial, because the Lab text covered a large part of the menu with many pop-ups. I would also add a ghost replay of my best run so I can learn better lines, and a small trajectory hint when jumping off a slope.

Quick facts: Mobile, 3D endless runner, Imangi Studios, 2011.

An explorer steals a cursed idol and is chased through temple ruins by demon monkeys. I chose it because it is free, it runs on mobile, and it clearly uses 3D vectors, a chase camera and pursuit. The monsters are always visible behind you, which keeps the tension constant.

Distance: Score grows with distance run (260 at the start of one run, 42,070 later). The gap between me and the monsters works like a danger value that likely shrinks after a stumble, and coins are picked up with a distance check. Direction and vectors: The player runs forward and turns 90 degrees at corners. Position updates each frame by velocity * time, and tilting the phone adds a sideways component. Algebra: Score, coins (0, then 279) and the achievement count (57) are running totals compared against thresholds. Dot product: Coins and obstacles ahead are relevant while the monsters are behind. A dot product between the forward vector and the vector to an object decides front or back. Cross product: At a corner the game must know if my swipe turns left or right and rotate the camera the same way. The sign of the cross product gives that direction. Lerp: Turns look smooth, the camera swings behind the player after each corner, and coins spin.

The camera sits behind and above the player. Each frame its target is:

camera_target = player_pos - forward * d + up * h

It doesn’t snap there. It moves toward it with lerp:

camera_pos = camera_pos + (camera_target - camera_pos) * t

When I turn at a corner, the forward vector rotates by 90 degrees and the camera swings round smoothly. This is what gives the long stone bridge such a strong sense of depth and speed.

What works well: The monsters behind you create real urgency, the swipe and tilt controls are intuitive, and the camera sells the speed.

What I would improve: Modernise the textures and character models, add daily challenges such as “collect 100 coins without jumping” for variety, and add a subtle screen-edge effect that grows as the monsters get closer so the chase distance is easier to read.

Lerp and algebra showed up the most across the three games. Lerp is behind the smooth lane changes in Subway Surfers, the animation blending in Vector and the camera swing in Temple Run, so almost every smooth motion on screen seems to use it. Algebra is in every score, multiplier, coin counter and mission bar. Distance was a close third, because pickups, chasers and obstacles all depend on how far apart things are.

Before this assignment I only noticed whether a game was fun. Now I notice why the camera lags slightly, why a character glides instead of jumping between positions, and how a simple multiplier shapes what I do next. Vectors and distance control movement and detection, dot and cross products handle direction, algebra drives scores and rewards, and lerp makes everything feel smooth. The best designs make that math invisible, and I can now imagine building these mechanics myself.

Watch my video walkthrough: https://youtu.be/Mz7PZpl1Eoo Screenshots from all three games: https://imgur.com/a/8Bx9eOZ

#9818. Is a gas oven bad for bread?: Why a gas oven may be interfering with your go-to steaming method.

Adapted from King Arthur Baking Company’s Big Book of Bread

One of the most crucial steps for making crusty artisan-style bread comes at the very end: steaming.

Baking bread with steam is critical for achieving expansive, open-crumbed loaves with a golden, crisp crust. If you bake bread in a dry oven, the crust quickly sets, which prevents the dough from expanding to its full potential; this, in turn, leads to loaves with a denser crumb. If you introduce steam at the start of the bake, the crust remains moist and pliable and the loaf can stretch and expand before the crust sets, resulting in a lighter, more open crumb.

What’s more, steam also helps gelatinize starches on the loaf’s exterior, which helps it brown and creates an especially crispy, flavorful, and shiny loaf. (Learn more: A guide to baking bread with steam at home.)

There are many different ways to steam your bread, all of which are designed to introduce moisture to the oven during the first part of baking. The most common method involves setting a large cast-iron skillet below your baking stone or steel when you preheat the oven. After you load your bread into the oven, you immediately pour a cup or so of warm water into the preheated cast-iron skillet and quickly close the door so the steam doesn’t escape.

This method works great, with one exception: It’s not effective in a gas oven.

If you have a gas oven, it’s very hard to add sufficient steam. By design, gas ovens vent out effluence, meaning whatever steam you add is very quickly vented out of the oven chamber. This is particularly true if you steam your bread by pouring hot water into a cast-iron skillet, as outlined above. All the water quickly dissipates, and there’s not enough moisture left to enhance the crust.

But all is not lost. There is a workaround.

If you’re steaming bread in a gas oven, you need to use a preheated covered baker, such as a Dutch oven. Instead of adding an additional water source, the lidded vessel traps the steam that escapes from the loaf as it bakes, becoming a kind of self-steaming oven. Because the steam is sealed in, the gas oven won’t vent it out.

You can use a Dutch oven for a round, boule-shaped loaf, or any other form of covered baker, like the Brod & Taylor Bread Steel for elongated, bâtard-shaped loaves. (There’s also a round version of the Bread Steel available.)

For more guidance on this method, see our previous blogs, Bread baking in a Dutch oven and For crispy, crackle crusts, put a lid on it.

When you load your dough into the oven, slip a few ice cubes between the parchment beneath your loaf and the pan to give the loaf an extra initial burst of steam. Just don’t skip the parchment beneath the dough. Otherwise, the extra water from the melting ice may cause your bread to stick to the pot.

#9817. Educational Byte: What Is a Liquidity Pool in Crypto —and Why It Matters

To understand this one, let’s first look at the "traditional" processes for exchanging money via digital platforms. We can commonly see two mechanisms: you exchange your currency directly against the exchange or provider’s own funds, or an order book is used. This order book records all buy and sell orders placed by users and provides liquidity based on that activity. The more orders in place, the more liquidity. Well, liquidity pools have come to replace these models in Decentralized Finance (DeFi) protocols.

A liquidity pool in crypto is a supply of tokens locked inside a smart contract on a DeFi protocol. It has the purpose of offering liquidity to other users for swaps, loans, or any financial activity on that specific protocol. The locked funds come from other users who, in exchange for providing this liquidity to the pool, receive rewards in the form of transaction fees and even governance tokens.

This way, no powerful middlemen are required to safely access financial instruments. It’s the users themselves who provide liquidity in a decentralized environment.

Typically, a liquidity pool holds two tokens, such as GBYTE and USDC. Liquidity providers are the ones who deposit these token pairs—and they could be anyone with the available funds. Then, those funds help to create a big reserve that traders can use for their own operations, like swaps. The smart contract keeps track of those balances and applies the rules that govern each trade.

Price adjustment comes from the reserves themselves. In a classic Automated Market Maker (AMM) model, a simple formula is used: X × Y = K, where X and Y represent the quantities of the two tokens and K is the constant. When someone swaps, let’s say, USDC for GBYTE, the pool receives one asset and releases the other, changing the balances and thus the price for the next trade. Depending on the available liquidity, a larger trade may create more price impact, which implies that the price could drop by a certain percentage for the next swap.

For liquidity providers, the platform may give them LP tokens as proof of their share of the pool. These tokens can be used to track and redeem that share, including the depositor’s portion of trading fees earned by the pool. Their reward is directly proportional to their contribution to the pool.

Some pools may be rewarded with additional incentives. For instance, in the Obyte-based DEX Oswap.io, all liquidity providers to a few selected pools receive 100 GBYTE every seven days, distributed in proportion to their contributed liquidity. That’s an additional incentive on top of fees.

A healthy financial environment needs liquidity, and liquidity doesn’t come out of nowhere. For trades and other operations to actually happen, funds must be available, and someone must put the funds there. In traditional finance, that someone is often a powerful middleman, like a bank. But cryptocurrencies weren’t created to rely on powerful middlemen; they were created to get rid of them. So, we have liquidity pools instead.

By using this model, everyone can access liquidity without cumbersome requirements or censorship risks. Meanwhile, liquidity providers receive rewards for their contributions in what is, without a doubt, a type of investment that can yield a good and frequent passive return. Of course, the specific rules and the censorship resistance vary from network to network.

Obyteuses a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) structure without miners or “validators,” which increases its decentralization and drastically reduces the mere possibility of censorship or blocking. In Oswap.io, each pool has its own parameters and governance, but all are decentralized and open for everyone to participate. That’s the whole idea; that’s why liquidity pools matter: they offer a freedom we can’t enjoy in traditional financial products.

#9815. How our Pipeline orchestrates LBO Due Diligence ?

Welcome to the third chapter of our four-part series, **Building Sovereign, Hallucination-Free Financial AI. In Part 1: Building a Deterministic Financial Agent with Dual-Persona LoRA, we prohibited probabilistic language models from performing arithmetic. In Part 2: How our Training Recipe led us to "Hallucination", we stepped into the machine room: fine-tuning an 8B model.

Today, we address the ultimate frontier: What happens when the financial question cannot fit into a single prompt or table? How do we orchestrate complex, multi-step workflows like a Cross-Table LBO Due Diligence across disparate financial statements—and how do we ensure the final synthesis sent to the boardroom is 100% immune to semantic inversion and hallucination?

In Part 2, we showed that when an 8B specialist model encounters missing variables in a messy financial filing, standard RLHF conditions it to panic: it grabs loosely related numbers from adjacent rows to satisfy the prompt, falling directly into the Compensation Hallucination Trap.

We fixed this at the micro-level with response-only masking and rejection circuit breakers. But in enterprise finance, you quickly encounter a macro-level barrier:

Imagine handing an autonomous agent an audited annual report (like the official French standalone filing — comptes sociaux — of Renault SAS, Renault Group's main operating subsidiary) and asking:

"Is a leveraged buyout (LBO) of this target financially feasible based on its latest audited accounts?"

Answering this is not a one-shot retrieval problem. It requires navigating across multiple disparate accounting schedules:

If you shove all these tables into a single context window and ask an 8B model to reason through all five steps at once, attention anxiety returns with a vengeance. The model conflates standalone operating subsidiary debt with consolidated group figures, divides equity by operating profit, or produces subtle, catastrophic semantic inversions.

To solve this, we must enforce Separation of Concerns at the system architecture level.

Instead of burdening a single specialist model with planning, document navigation, tool invocation, and narrative synthesis, we architected a Bilateral Multi-Agent Hierarchy governed by Domain-Driven Design (DDD).

What is a Multi-Step DAG? A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) is a deterministic task pipeline where execution flows strictly forward from prerequisites to dependent outputs (Directed) with zero infinite loops (Acyclic). Independent balance sheet extractions run in parallel, while cross-table ratios wait for their exact upstream inputs before converging into the final decision policy.

The Specialist Advisor does not write paragraphs of text. Its sole responsibility is to evaluate available physical table rubrics against declarative banking covenants:

When the Generalist Crew Manager receives the LBO query, it feeds the extracted table headers to the Specialist, which compiles an ExecutionPlanDTO composed of 5 non-negotiable credit pillars:

Because each task has designated keywords and an explicit formula, the tasks execute sequentially or in parallel against our Physical Grounding Engine.

As established in Part 1, all tool calls are executed in Python using exact Decimal arithmetic.

In our Renault SAS 2024 benchmark test (LOGS_ECHANGE_GEN_SPEC_LBO_RENAULT.md), the runtime produces audited outputs anchored to exact physical lines:

The arithmetic outcome is definitive: 8.50 years of cash flow are required to extinguish existing debt. According to LboCovenantPolicyVO ($> 5.0\text{ years}$), an LBO without massive capital restructuring is strictly unfeasible.

Now comes the ultimate vulnerability: How do we guarantee the LLM does not distort this finding when writing the final executive briefing?

Most agent frameworks rely on the LLM's own self-critique (e.g., "Review your previous response and fix any errors"). As research has repeatedly demonstrated, this triggers sycophancy and confirmation bias: the model rationalizes its mistakes rather than catching them.

What does GenRM stand for? GenRM stands for Generative Reward Model—an adversarial verifier pattern introduced in Generative Verifiers: Reward Modeling as Next-Token Prediction (arXiv:2408.15240). While frameworks like NVIDIA's post-training pipeline for Nemotron-3.5-Bolt use GenRM at train time (RLHF/RLVR alignment), we apply the same generative verifier pattern at inference time inside a 2-Layer Hybrid Neuro-Symbolic GenRMCritic with absolute veto power before any memo reaches the C-suite.

To achieve true enterprise readiness without relying on fragile regexes alone—and without wasting GPU cycles on obvious arithmetic errors—we architected GenRMCritic as a two-stage neuro-symbolic gatekeeper:

Every percentage extracted from the draft memo must match a certified result in the FinancialRuntime registry within a $0.05\%$ margin. If the model hallucinates "an operating margin of 42.5%" when the certified runtime output was -18.47%, Layer 1 issues an immediate VETO with zero LLM calls.

The most insidious failure in financial AI is directional polarity inversion or strategic verdict contradiction expressed with unexpected phrasing.

Consider these real adversarial cases verified against live Nemotron 3.5 Bolt in our E2E benchmark:

Here is our production 2-layer GenRMCritic implementation (with an offline deterministic fallback when no GPU/model backend is injected):

When a VETO is issued, the Generalist Crew Manager initiates a single targeted correction turn, injecting the explicit rejection reason into the synthesizer's context.

When all gates clear, the engine outputs an auditable, executive-ready memorandum. Below is the actual verbatim output (synthese_complete) generated end-to-end by our live Nemotron 3.5 Bolt pipeline + Python IEEE-754 runtime + Hybrid Neuro-Symbolic GenRMCritic on Renault SAS's audited 2024 standalone accounts (comptes sociaux, elapsed_s: 104.08s, certified_count: 4, genrm_calls: 2, GenRM verdict: [PASS]):

(Note on the 2024 figures: On Renault SAS's standalone 2024 accounts, CAF rose +83.02% from €1,378M to €2,522M while Financial Debt fell -37.55% from €7,487M to €4,676M, bringing Debt/CAF down to 1.85x and Gearing to 55.2% — clearing LboCovenantPolicyVO thresholds as FAVORABLE, whereas earlier 2023 standalone debt levels of €10,587M vs. €1,245M CAF yielded 8.50x and UNFAVORABLE.)

Deploying LLMs in regulated, mission-critical environments (finance, medical, legal) requires abandoning several common AI tropes:

#9814. Ahrefs vs SEMrush: Which SEO Tool Should You Use?

SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month.

If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist.

In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.

SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database.

The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension

Ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The company was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database.

Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis.

Ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need quickly.

In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks.

The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs.

Additional features of the Ahrefs platform include:

When you log into the SEMrush Tool, you will find four main modules. These include information about your domains, organic keyword analysis, ad keyword, and site traffic.

Both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources.

When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both.

If you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors.

Let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job.

The Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter.

Rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers:

You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty.

It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not.

SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a new project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool:

The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking.

Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages.

Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report.

Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords.

SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment.

Keyword research is closely related to rank tracking, but it's used for deciding which keywords you plan on using for future content rather than those you use now.

When it comes to SEO, keyword research is the most important thing to consider when comparing the two platforms.

The Ahrefs Keyword Explorer provides you with thousands of keyword ideas and filters search results based on the chosen search engine.

Ahrefs supports several features, including:

SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool has over 20 billion keywords for Google. You can type in any keyword you want, and a list of suggested keywords will appear.

Both of these tools offer keyword research features and allow users to break down complicated tasks into something that can be understood by beginners and advanced users alike.

If you're interested in keyword suggestions, SEMrush appears to have more keyword suggestions than Ahrefs does. It also continues to add new features, like the Keyword Gap tool and SERP Questions recommendations.

Both platforms offer competitor analysis tools, eliminating the need to come up with keywords off the top of your head. Each tool is useful for finding keywords that will be useful for your competition so you know they will be valuable to you.

Ahrefs' domain comparison tool lets you compare up to five websites (your website and four competitors) side-by-side.it also shows you how your site is ranked against others with metrics such as backlinks, domain ratings, and more.

Use the Competing Domains section to see a list of your most direct competitors, and explore how many keywords matches your competitors have.

To find more information about your competitor, you can look at the Site Explorer and Content Explorer tools and type in their URL instead of yours.

SEMrush provides a variety of insights into your competitors' marketing tactics. The platform enables you to research your competitors effectively. It also offers several resources for competitor analysis including:

Traffic Analytics helps you identify where your audience comes from, how they engage with your site, what devices visitors use to view your site, and how your audiences overlap with other websites.

SEMrush's Organic Research examines your website's major competitors and shows their organic search rankings, keywords they are ranking for, and even if they are ranking for any (SERP) features and more.

The Market Explorer search field allows you to type in a domain and lists websites or articles similar to what you entered. Market Explorer also allows users to perform in-depth data analytics on These companies and markets.

SEMrush wins here because it has more tools dedicated to competitor analysis than Ahrefs. However, Ahrefs offers a lot of functionality in this area, too. It takes a combination of both tools to gain an advantage over your competition.

When it comes to keyword data research, you will become confused about which one to choose.

Both tools are great. Choose the one which meets your requirements and if you have any experience using either Ahrefs or SEMrush let me know in the comment section which works well for you.

#9811. Zillow for-sale, rental and sold listings with n8n (free workflow)

Get Zillow for-sale, rental and sold listings into n8n with prices, property details and listing URLs. Import the workflow, add your Apify token as a Query Auth credential, and edit Configure input. A first run returning 25 rows costs about $0.42 on Apify’s Free plan, plus platform compute usage.

Disclosure: I maintain the free MIT workflow and skill repos, and scraping runs a public Apify Actor on your own Apify account as paid usage. This article was drafted with AI help, with every field, setting and price checked against the repo files and the Actor’s pricing.

When a portal email arrives after a price cut, your shortlist is already behind. Bring the listings into your daily review so you can compare price, status and daysOnZillow together.

The workflow searches by city, state or ZIP for active listings, rentals or recently sold properties. Its main output fields are:

The wider output includes zestimate, rentZestimate, agentName, agentPhone, agentEmail, schools, priceHistory and taxHistory. Use populated fields from the returned rows when building your destination mapping.

For a comps review, keep the property details beside soldPrice, dateSold and url. For an active-listing review, start with price, daysOnZillow and priceChange. Keep the URL so you can open the property before acting on a row.

You can finish at Rows ready if another downstream step will consume the rows. The sheet is an optional destination.

Set mode to BUY, RENT or SOLD. The default is BUY, which is also what the starter uses.

To narrow a location search, add priceMin, priceMax, bedsMin, bathsMin, sqftMin or sqftMax to the input. Bedroom and bathroom minimums are strings. For example, use "bedsMin": "2" or "bathsMin": "1.5".

maxItems limits the whole run across all sources. Its schema default is 50, and its allowed range is 1 to 5000. The starter explicitly overrides it.

endPage limits search-result pages per search task. It defaults to 5 and accepts 1 to 24. Zillow returns up to 41 listings per page. These are collection limits, so use them to control scope without assuming every search will fill the requested maximum.

On Apify’s Free plan, the Actor charges a start event per GB of run memory, then a fee for each result. Platform compute is billed on top and has no fixed price in this estimate.

The Actor’s default is 4096 MB, or 4 GB. The workflow leaves memory unset so that default applies. Keep it unchanged.

A daily run returning 25 rows for 30 days comes to about $12.74 before compute. The Free plan includes $5.00 in credit, which covers about 11 such runs before compute is added. Paid plans have lower Actor event prices. Check Apify pricing when budgeting recurring usage.

Normalize + dedupe trims strings, drops empty values, adds _source and _scrapedAt, and keeps one row per url in the data it processes.

The URL gives you a reference back to the listing when reviewing the cleaned rows. Keep it in your destination even if the visible report mainly shows addresses and prices.

For recurring appends, keep _scrapedAt alongside url so you can distinguish captures when comparing a property over time. Normalization prepares the rows. Any comparison between captures belongs in your downstream review or processing.

If Apify returns an error object, the workflow stops with Apify’s message instead of writing it as a listing row. Read that message before changing your input.

The synchronous request waits up to 300 seconds, and the HTTP node timeout is 300000 milliseconds. If the request times out, inspect the run in your Apify account before launching another paid start.

If the output does not match your intended search, check the input route. Search URLs supplied through startUrls retain their own filters and mode.

If you are weighing alternatives, this comparison page compares the other tools and the official API for Zillow by output fields and price per 1,000 results.

Can I use this on n8n Cloud or self-hosted n8n?

Yes. It uses core nodes: Schedule Trigger, Code, HTTP Request, No Operation and Google Sheets.

Can I provide known properties instead of searching an area?

Yes. Use zpids for Zillow property IDs, or addresses for full street addresses. Each ZPID resolves to its canonical detail page.

Yes. startUrls accepts property detail URLs, /apartments/ building URLs and Zillow search page URLs.

The workflow and skill files are MIT licensed and free to use. Running the public Actor incurs usage charges on your Apify account.

Does the imported JSON include an API token?

No. The files contain no token or credential. Add your own credential during setup.

And the best part? Starting your business can be done in just five minutes.

Sellfy is an eCommerce solution that allows digital content creators, including writers, illustrators, designers, musicians, and filmmakers, to sell their products online. Sellfy product pages enable users to showcase their products from different angles with multiple images and previews from Soundcloud, Vimeo, and YouTube. Sellfy also allows you to create a full shopping cart so customers can purchase multiple items. And Sellfy gives you the ability to set your language or let customers see a translated version of your store based on their location.

Sellfy gives you the option to host your store directly on its platform, add a custom domain to your store, and use it as an embedded storefront on your website. Sellfy also optimizes its store offerings for mobile devices, allowing for a seamless checkout experience.

Sellfy also does not place storage limits on your store but recommends that files be no larger than 5GB. Sellfy offers several ways to share your store, enabling you to promote your business on different platforms. Sellfy lets you integrate it with your existing website using "buy now" buttons, embed your entire storefront, or embed certain products so you can reach more people. Sellfy also enables you to connect with your Facebook page and YouTube channel, maximizing your visibility.

Sellfy is a simple online platform that allows customers to buy your products directly through your store. Sellfy has two payment processing options: PayPal and Stripe. You will receive instant payments with both of these processors, and your customer data is protected by Sellfy's secure (PCI-compliant) payment security measures. In addition to payment security, Sellfy provides anti-fraud tools to help protect your products including PDF stamping, unique download links, and limited download attempts.

To expand functionality and make your e-commerce store run more efficiently, Sellfy offers several integrations. Sellfy allows you to connect to Zapier, which gives you access to hundreds of third-party apps, including tools like Mailchimp, Trello, Salesforce, and more.

Sellfy has its benefits and downsides, but fortunately, the pros outweigh the cons.

#9807. The Digital Euro: Solving Problems You Didn’t Have, With Rules You Don’t Write

Do you actually need a digital euro because payments weren’t convenient enough already?

I pay for everything with my phone. Instantly. Even when I’m abroad. To be fair, I’m still glad we actually get to live in the 21st century.

And no, it’s not because they want to ban cash. Cash is already quietly fading out of daily use in Europe. It’s certainly not because someone at a central bank suddenly developed a burning passion for transparency and democratisation.

So let’s look at what’s actually being built, who gets to set the rules, and most importantly, why it’s being built at all.

(It’s just the rehearsal where nobody gets to leave)

According to ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone’s speech on 5 November 2026, they plan a 12-month pilot in the second half of 2027.

It will involve 36 payment service providers, including Deutsche Bank, UniCredit, Revolut, Stripe, and Adyen. Testing will cover ordinary situations: purchases, transfers, and refunds.

According to the ECB, the target for a possible first issuance is 2029, but only if the necessary legislation is adopted by the end of 2026. Only then would the Governing Council decide whether to issue it at all.

Preparing a system and approving its use are two separate decisions. News headlines tend to treat them as the same thing.

It might come as a shock, but the balance you see in your banking app isn’t actually your money. It’s a promise from your local bank that they’ll repay it one day. A digital euro would move that promise even further away, all the way behind the walls of the ECB headquarters in Frankfurt.

Apart from that minor detail, your brand-new digital euro would be almost identical to what you already use.

It would still be worth one euro. It would still appear on your screen as if you owned it. And it would still not be immune to money printing, inflation, or devaluation.

Under the proposed design it wouldn’t even pay the princely 0.05% interest some accounts currently offer. And there would be a limit on how much you could hold. Roughly €3,000 was one of the options analysed, not a final rule.

Now, to be fair, there is one legitimate point in favor of the digital euro.

For card payments, Europe still depends heavily on non-European companies, in practice, mainly Visa and Mastercard. A shared European payments infrastructure makes sense as a political and economic objective. The real test is whether regular people actually get enough out of the digital euro to bother switching.

Good luck convincing 450 million people to just switch up their daily habits. Especially when the new system arrives with holding limits, no interest, and a few extra questions about why you’re using it.

That does not mean the entire wallet would operate anonymously like cash. Anti-money-laundering checks would still apply when depositing, transferring or withdrawing funds.

In other words, the ECB says it will not monitor everything you buy. Your local bank will.

The ECB says the digital euro would not be programmable money. The issuer wouldn’t dictate where, when or on what you could spend it. That’s different from a conditional payment you choose to arrange yourself.

So there’s no need for panic about your money expiring or a sudden ban on steak purchases.

There is a good reason to check whether protection against such restrictions remains firmly written into the final rules. A press release is no substitute for a legal safeguard.

The same applies to cash. The ECB says the digital euro would complement it, not replace it. What matters is whether people can actually keep using cash, and whether pulling it out of your wallet is still treated as normal rather than vaguely suspicious.

The digital euro and Bitcoin serve different purposes.

A digital euro would remain a euro, governed by monetary and public institutions.

As I learned the hard way after a single copy-paste mistake sent a test transfer straight into oblivion: with Bitcoin, I don’t need a central issuer to hold or send my money. The catch? If I hold my own keys, protecting them is entirely on me.

Bitcoin isn’t magically anonymous, either. Its public ledger and wild price swings don’t vanish just because we’re fed up with central banks.

I judge the digital euro on whether it actually fixes payments without chipping away at our rights. I judge Bitcoin on its own merits and risks. They’re playing entirely different games.

The digital euro isn’t about easier coffee purchases.

Once the rules are written and the system is live, complaining that “this wasn’t what we signed up for” will be largely irrelevant.

The real question isn’t whether the digital euro happens.

It’s whether we wake up in time to realize our right to use our own money is being quietly rewritten. Politely, step by step, and backed by world-class PR.

Bitcoin Is Not Just an Investment. It’s an Escape Hatch From the Financial Gulag

#9806. I built a PDF toolkit that never uploads your files

Posted on Nov 13 • Originally published at convup.lodcrafttools.workers.dev

Every "free" PDF converter I tried asked me to upload the file first. For a bank statement or a signed contract, that is the whole problem: you are handing a document to a server you know nothing about, and hoping it gets deleted.

So I built ConvUp, a converter that runs entirely in the browser. No upload endpoint, no account, no watermark.

The only network requests are the app's own static files and, for OCR, the Tesseract language model from a public CDN. Your document never appears in any request. That is verifiable: open DevTools, go to Network, convert a file.

The first tool I wrote was "rotate pages". It is four lines:

No pixels are touched. A PDF page carries a rotation attribute that the viewer applies when drawing; changing it fixes a sideways scan without recompressing anything, so text stays selectable and images keep their resolution.

That distinction matters: most online tools re-render the page to an image and hand you back a heavier, blurrier file.

1. Scanned PDFs. A scan has no text layer. Converting it to Word gives you an empty document. The honest fix is OCR first, then convert — and even then, accuracy depends on 300 dpi, straight pages and printed text. Handwriting and shadows still fail.

2. Multi-column layouts. A PDF does not store paragraphs; it stores text fragments at coordinates. To rebuild a document you group fragments by baseline and guess the reading order. Single column: fine. Two or three columns, tables, footers mixed into the body: the order comes out scrambled and needs manual fixes. I decided not to pretend otherwise and said so in the UI.

3. Memory. Everything happens in the tab. A 200 MB audio file or a 600-page scan can kill it. The limits (15 minutes of audio, 40 PDFs to merge, 500 MB per file) exist because the browser is the machine doing the work.

Local processing means the user's device pays the cost. A 40-page scanned PDF compressed in the browser takes seconds to minutes depending on the CPU, while a server farm would do it in one. I think it is the right trade for documents you would not email to a stranger, but it is a trade.

The site is free and has ads. They load when you open a tool, and in the EU, the UK and Switzerland only after you accept. No pop-ups on the homepage, no forced clicks, no "wait 30 seconds to download". The file is generated before any ad gate.

If you want to try it: convup.lodcrafttools.workers.dev. If something breaks, tell me which file and what you expected — I would rather fix a real failure than add a feature nobody asked for.

#9805. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.

As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.

This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.

Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.

Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.

Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.

whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.

Their UI most definitely could use improvement, but these changes are not great improvements; they only serve to confuse users. Their resources would be better spent fixing the many functional problems in their app.- Some of Pro Writing Aid's checks are completely useless, as they do not take context into consideration. For example, an ordinary word would not be capitalized as part of a narrative, but would be as part of a title (for example, "professor." But if you capitalize correctly for context, Pro Writing Aid dings you for "Inconsistent capitalization." Similar issues exist with hyphenation consistency check.Each of these applications has its strengths as well as considerable weaknesses. I will say that both of them are light-years better than the execrable grammar checker in Microsoft Word, but that's damning with faint praise.

#9802. Reading a webhook debugging prompt line by line

Webhook bugs are awkward to hand to an AI. The symptom shows up in one place, while the cause sits in delivery order, retries or a recent change somewhere else. This is a teardown of a prompt from the PromptAlo community library built for exactly that: Finding Why Third-Party Webhook Events Arrive Out of Order.

Solves: Backend developers whose app breaks when webhooks arrive late, twice or in the wrong order.

Three failure modes in one sentence: late, duplicated and reordered. Naming all of them matters, because a fix for order alone will not stop the same event being processed again.

Fill in these variables: [APP], [FLOW], [SYMPTOMS], [RETRIES], [LOGS], [CHANGES]

[FLOW] is the field that shapes the answer. The prompt asks the model to map it and mark where order is assumed, so each assumption can be checked against the event ids in [SYMPTOMS]. [RETRIES] and [CHANGES] point it at the common causes, and [LOGS] come with personal data removed, so customer payloads stay out of the conversation.

How to adapt: For email events or IoT device messages, swap the provider. If order does not matter, focus on idempotency only.

The second sentence is the practical one. Not every integration cares about order, and when it does not, the work shrinks to handling the same event more than once without side effects.

The output is a flow with order assumptions, ranked causes, a logging plan, handling rules, shuffled replay tests and a rollout check. The constraints prefer simple version checks over complex buffers, and ask for a [CONFIRM] marker wherever provider docs need checking instead of a guess.

#9801. Tech Adoption Is a Cultural Problem: Why UX Habits Beat Innovation

Oh no, sweetheart. Culture doesn’t adapt to your technology.

Stop blaming Mercury in retrograde when users refuse to abandon their old habits for your shiny new tool. The pattern is always the same: the best tool in the room loses to the one people already trust. Founders file this failure under pricing, onboarding, or "users who need education." In reality, it belongs under culture.

My name is Daria. I help tech companies explain what makes their products different and why they matter. At university, I studied sociology and cultural studies. It taught me to look at people in groups first, and products second.

Look at the current wave of AI: the Humane AI Pin had stellar backers, deep pockets, and massive hype. It was dead in a year. ChatGPT was a plain text box, and it became the fastest-growing app in history. Same period, same underlying tech, and culture decided which one survived.

In 2020, a Japanese minister went to war on two office objects: the fax machine and the hanko, the small personal seal people stamp in red ink instead of signing.

Taro Kono (Minister for Digital Transformation of Japan) had the power and the better technology. A signed PDF is faster, cheaper, and easier to search than a stamped fax. He got most government offices to agree to drop the seal. Years later, the fax still hums and the seal still sits in the drawer.

The seal survived because in Japan it was never only a tool. It stands for identity and consent. A company, a bank, and a neighbor all read it the same way. A better tool cannot push out a habit the whole country trusts.

In China, credit cards never caught on; by 2021 only about 38 percent of adults had one. So people skipped the card and went from cash straight to the QR code.

Today two apps, Alipay and WeChat Pay, handle more than nine in ten mobile payments, from the fruit stall to the temple donation box.

The same thing happens inside companies now. A team gets a powerful new AI tool, and people keep working the old way, because the old way is the one they trust.

How did ChatGPT manage to become so popular and usher in a new era of consumer AI? People already knew how to type a question into a box, the way they type into Google or a chat with a friend.

More than a million people tried it in five days. Around 100 million were using it two months after launch. TikTok took nine months to reach that number. Instagram took more than two years.

ChatGPT did not ask us to adopt a new habit or buy a new device. The company didn't ruin our familiar flow.

The Humane AI Pin launched in 2024 with huge attention. It clipped to your shirt, had no screen, and answered out loud or showed tiny text on your palm. To use it, people had to wear a new device, learn new hand gestures, and talk to their own chest in public.

By the summer, the company was taking back more pins each day than it sold. In 2025, HP bought what was left for 116 million dollars and switched the pins off.

The Rabbit R1, another AI gadget from the same year, got the same cold response. Both asked people to build a habit from zero, with nothing pushing them to do it.

Great tech can still misjudge the culture it lands in. In February 2024, Google added image generation to Gemini. Asked for pictures of people from history, it often returned images that did not match the record. The reaction was loud and fast. Within days, Google paused the feature for images of people. The fix took months.

The temptation for founders and product builders is always to focus on the raw technology: the compute power, the model architecture, the sheer wizardry of what a tool can do. But history rewards the technology that integrates seamlessly into how humans already behave.

If you are building something new, you have only two choices:

Tech fails when it assumes people will change their culture just to use a clever tool. Culture is stubborn, patient, and deeply rooted. Ignore human behavior, and your brilliant creation will end up abandoned.

#9799. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

Find our high-extraction Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour online.

#9798. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. #9797. .NET 8 support ended on 10 November: a migration checklist for WinForms, WPF and Office add-ins

.NET 8 and .NET 9 stopped getting security patches on 10 November 2026. .NET 10 is the current LTS and is supported until November 2028.

Most upgrade guides are about ASP.NET. Desktop apps break in different places: the clipboard, designer resources, third-party controls, installers and Office add-ins. Here is the checklist I use for WinForms and WPF apps, roughly in the order things go wrong.

Open each .csproj and look at the target:

Run dotnet --list-runtimes on a typical user machine too. You will often find several runtimes installed that nobody remembers adding.

A framework-dependent .NET 8 app will not start on the .NET 10 runtime by default. If you can't migrate this month, you can let it run on a newer major version:

This is a stopgap, not a migration. The app still runs code compiled against .NET 8 APIs, and every behaviour change in steps 3 to 5 can hit you at runtime instead of at compile time. Test it before you ship it.

Add a global.json so that everyone on the team, and your CI, builds with the same SDK:

If you use Directory.Build.props, change the target framework there once instead of in 40 project files.

BinaryFormatter was removed in .NET 9. If you skipped .NET 9, this is the change that will hurt the most. Look for:

Replace it with System.Text.Json. For data files you have to read again, write a one-time converter before you remove the old code path.

In .NET 10, Clipboard.GetData and DataObject.GetData are obsolete (warning WFDEV005). Worse, Clipboard.SetData with a custom type now fails silently: nothing lands on the clipboard and no exception is thrown.

Search the whole solution for GetData( and SetData(, including in-app copy and paste between grids. Users notice this one first.

Two .NET 10 SDK changes break builds that use TreatWarningsAsErrors:

DevExpress, Telerik, Infragistics, Syncfusion and others support new runtimes only in newer releases. Before you start:

Old abandoned controls with no .NET 10 build are the most common reason a "one-day retarget" turns into a project.

Then you also need SDK-style project files, packages.config converted to PackageReference, app.config settings reviewed, and WCF clients moved to the System.ServiceModel.* packages. Some APIs simply don't exist anymore (AppDomains, .NET Remoting, parts of System.Web). Do an assessment before you estimate anything.

About tools: Microsoft has deprecated the .NET Upgrade Assistant in favour of GitHub Copilot app modernization, which needs a paid Copilot plan. The old Upgrade Assistant can still be turned on in Visual Studio 2026 (Tools > Options > Projects and Solutions > Modernization). Both handle the mechanical part well. Neither one knows that your grid vendor changed an event signature.

For a .NET 8 app with modern dependencies, all of this is usually a day or two of work. For a .NET Framework app with old third-party controls, COM interop and an add-in or two, it is a project, and a short assessment before you start saves the most time.

If you'd like a second pair of eyes on your solution, we do fixed-price WinForms and WPF migration assessments at IntellyCode. Questions are welcome in the comments, too.
